title: Pilot bench compare vs baseline - ZenithCare weekly sync
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing latency/throughput benchmarks vs their current baseline provider. Redwood SE explains p50/p95 numbers, KV cache and batching tuning; customer requests follow-up runs with KV caching and a dedicated routing policy. Action items assigned and security/SSO reminder noted.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing for consistency
Security docs and next steps for pilot expansion
action_items: Priya - run 1k sample inference with prefix KV cache enabled and 4-bit quantized model; include P50/P95/P99 and tail latency histograms (due: 2025-10-10)
Raj - provision a small Dedicated test pool and share access details (due: 2025-10-13)
Jordan - send updated pricing spreadsheet with dedicated commit scenarios and burst pricing link (due: 2025-10-09)
Maya - provide 2000-record production-like prompt set & a baseline call log from current provider (due: 2025-10-09)
next_steps: Redwood to run KV-cache-enabled benchmark and compare to last week's cold-run numbers
Customer to spin up dedicated test pool and provide prompts/logs
Schedule a 30-min deep-dive on routing & fallback policies next Thursday
Share SOC2 + network diagram and SSO/SAML notes via secure link
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-10-07 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Narayanan (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (ZenithCare ML), Raj Singh (ZenithCare Infra), Laura Chen (ZenithCare PM)

[00:00] Jordan: All right folks, thanks for jumping on. Quick check — audio okay for everyone?
[00:05] Maya: Yep good here.
[00:07] Raj: Good.
[00:09] Jordan: Cool. Agenda: run through the latest bench results Priya ran, highlight gaps vs your baseline, and agree next runs and responsibilities. Priya, you want to start?
[00:20] Priya: Yeah, yeah. So I uploaded the deck and the raw csvs to the pilot folder — link is in the chat, deck: https://redwood.app/zenith/pilot-results (note: internal access) — and the headline is: our 1k sample with cold cache shows median around 42ms p50, p95 is 210, p99 480 on our hosted config using the quantized 4-bit variant. That's with default batching (auto batched at 32ms window) and no prefix KV cache. The customer's baseline, per the logs you shared, shows p50 38ms, p95 320, p99 850. So median is comparable, but tail is much better on our run.
[01:05] Maya: Wait -- your p95 is 210 vs their 320? That seems promising. But how were warm vs cold runs handled? Their baseline has a warm cache on some endpoints.
[01:15] Priya: Good question. Our first sweep was intentionally mixed — some cold starts. I also ran a dedicated-warm run where we preloaded KV for 10% of prompts: warm p50 36ms, p95 160. So enabling KV cache gives a big tail improvement. The tradeoff is memory use on the server side.
[01:35] Raj: When you say KV, do you mean the prefix kv cache, like the K-V cash? (laugh)
[01:39] Priya: (laughs) The K-V cash. Yes, KV cache. We'll send the config snippet. It's in the deck under 'Cache configs'.
[01:44] Laura: How deterministic are those improvements? We saw big variance last week with SaturaCloud that would spike unpredictably.
[01:52] Priya: We measured across five 1k samples over three hours. Variance decreased with dedicated pools and with smaller batching windows. There's a chart (slide 6) showing p99 histogram over time; spikes correlate with competing batch arrivals. The solution is routing and isolation or smaller batch ticks.
[02:10] Jordan: To clarify — baseline provider (you called them BigCompute in prior notes) tends to have higher tail because they use larger batching windows to maximize throughput. Our approach lets you tune the batching window and commit to Dedicated for predictable tail.
[02:25] Maya: Can you share numbers for throughput? We need to ensure we meet the 250 reqs/sec target for peak loads.
[02:31] Priya: Sure. With hosted shared pool, peak sustainable throughput for a single GPU instance with our 4-bit quantized model was ~180 rps at p95 under steady state. With dedicated pool of 2 GPUs and middle-of-the-road batching (20ms tick) we simulated ~420 rps with p95 at 240ms. So dedicated seems to meet your 250 reqs/sec target comfortably with headroom.
[02:56] Raj: Those sim numbers assume continuous traffic patterns. We have bursty traffic — are there autoscaling/burst options?
[03:03] Carlos: Yep, Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscale policies; we can pre-warm additional nodes for predicted windows. We'll include the autoscale policy examples in the doc I share.
[03:12] Maya: Do you have any end-to-end cost numbers versus SaturaCloud? We need ballpark TCO.
[03:17] Jordan: We're working on updated pricing scenarios; I'll send the spreadsheet with reserved commit options and burst rates. For the same sustained load, dedicated commit worked out about 18% cheaper in our model due to better per-token efficiency with quantization and optimized kernels, but we'll send detailed math.
[03:32] Laura: On security, last time you mentioned SOC2 and SSO. We need the network diagram and the SAML flow for private deployments.
[03:40] Carlos: Got it — I'll drop SOC2 and the network diagram in the secure folder. SSO/SAML steps are in our security pack. Also note Private (VPC) option supports KMS integration.
[03:50] Raj: KMS — do you support our HSM vendor Trezor...Trezzor? (unclear)
[03:55] Carlos: We integrate with standard cloud KMS and customer-managed HSMs via the Private package; we'll confirm vendor compatibility and include a short matrix.
[04:05] Priya: Back to bench numbers — I want to highlight cold-start penalties. Cold-run p99 can be as high as 900ms for some sequences on non-quantized fallback paths; with quantized it was 480ms. So quantization + KV cache is the winning combo for tail latency.
[04:23] Maya: Do you have any qualitative difference in generation quality with 4-bit quant? We cannot degrade top-line NPS of the model.
[04:30] Priya: We ran the standard rouge/bleu-like evals on your prompt set; delta in quality metrics was within noise for your dialog workload. There's one prompt family where tokenization changes slightly affect very long context completions — I'll label that as 'needs human review' in the results.
[04:47] Laura: Can we see the specific prompts where quality diverges?
[04:50] Priya: Yes — action item for Maya to surface a 2k prompts slice that covers those long context cases.
[04:55] Maya: Yep will do.
[04:56] 
[05:00] [05:00] Jordan: Let's talk about the comparison to customer baseline — what else should we run to make this apples-to-apples?
[05:06] Raj: We need a run with the same warm/cold profile: 70/30 warm-to-cold, same prompt mixes, and identical concurrency. Also include their current time-to-first-byte measurements (TTFB).
[05:17] Priya: Agreed. We'll mirror their baseline run. Also we'll try a 'tuned' run: dedicated 2xGPU, KV enabled, quantized 4-bit, small tick window — that'll be our best-effort to beat their tail plus throughput.
[05:31] Maya: On measurement, can you provide raw latency logs? Their infra team wants to ingest them into Grafana for side-by-side.
[05:38] Priya: Yes — CSVs plus a Prometheus export are available. I'll send the Prom endpoint sample.
[05:43] Raj: A quick question about routing: If we do dedicated for a subset of tenancy, can we have fallback to hosted if capacity spikes? We want graceful degradation, not errors.
[05:53] Priya: Yes, Redwood routing policies support tiered fallback: try dedicated, if queue depth exceeds threshold or latency SLO breached, spill to hosted lower-cost instance or a cheaper model variant. You can define priority rules per route.
[06:06] Laura: Does that involve stateful session problems — like KV cache won't exist on fallback?
[06:10] Priya: Correct — fallback will lose KV/local cache benefits; you need to consider degraded SLOs on fallback. We can create sticky routing policies that preserve session affinity to reduce misses.
[06:21] Jordan: Any blockers from your side on the pilot?
[06:24] Raj: Only that we need controlled network access to the test cluster — I'll provision a jump host and share IPs. Also would like a small VPN tunnel for the private test, if possible.
[06:36] Carlos: We'll coordinate on network connection; note Private deployment is a separate onboarding but for a short Dedicated test pool we can do secure peering.
[06:44] Maya: Quick nit — some of the metric names in your csv didn't map exactly to our ingestion schema; e.g., you use 'lat_ms' vs our 'latency_ms'. Minor but worth aligning.
[06:54] Priya: Good catch; we'll normalize column names in the next drop.
[06:58] 
[07:02] [07:02] Priya: I'm going to read a quick set of numbers slide-by-slide: Slide 3 is the baseline compare, numbers we already glanced at. Slide 4 shows warm-run with KV enabled. Slide 5 is throughput scaling on 2xGPU Dedicated sim. Slide 6 histogram of p99 across the five runs. Slide 7 is cost model.
[07:22] Maya: On cost model, please include per-100k tokens cost and per-hour instance cost so we can translate to our billing.
[07:29] Jordan: We'll add a per-100k tokens line items.
[07:31] 
[07:35] [07:35] Raj: I want to call out that their baseline provider had higher p99 in midnight hours — we suspect noisy neighbors on their multi-tenant pool. Would running Dedicated during those windows be recommended?
[07:47] Priya: Yes. Dedicated removes noisy neighbor risk. Also we've seen consistent lower variance when we pin instances.
[07:54] Laura: Any compliance/regulatory concerns for us when using KV cache? We store small customer prefixes and partial transcribed context.
[08:02] Carlos: KV entries are ephemeral and can be configured for TTLs; for regulated workloads you can enable Private with customer-managed keys to ensure encryption at rest under your KMS. We'll add that to the security note.
[08:14] Maya: One more: baseline provider claims they do a multi-model sharding technique; does Redwood do model sharding or are we single model per GPU?
[08:23] Priya: Redwood runtime supports model parallelism and sharding for very large models, but for your model size we run single-model-per-GPU with kernel-level optimizations; sharding isn't necessary and would add comb complexity unless you go to the very large models.
[08:35] 
[08:40] [08:40] Jordan: Okay let's confirm next runs. Priya run A: mirror baseline profile (70/30 warm/cold), same prompt mix, CSV logs. Priya run B: tuned dedicated 2xGPU w/ KV + quantized 4-bit, small batching window. Raj to provision dedicated test pool and network. Maya to provide 2k prompt slice and baseline logs. Jordan to send pricing. Carlos to share SOC2 and network diagram. Any objections?
[09:07] Maya: No objections. Sounds good.
[09:09] Raj: One thought — can we get an additional run with fallback enabled to see degraded SLO behavior?
[09:14] Priya: Yep we'll include a fallback simulation in run B2.
[09:18] Laura: And let's try to have that deep-dive on routing next Thursday at 10am PT.
[09:23] Jordan: I'll schedule it.
[09:25] 
[09:28] [09:28] Jordan: Quick recap and responsibilities: Priya will run three bench scenarios and drop CSVs + Prom exporter; Raj will provision Dedicated access; Maya provides prompts and baseline call logs; Jordan sends pricing; Carlos sends security pack. We'll reconvene after Prairie's runs — sorry Priya — after Priya's runs are uploaded.
[09:48] Priya: (laughs) that's fine.
[09:51] Jordan: Anything else?
[09:53] Maya: If you could flag any prompts where quality drops on quantized, that'd help our PM triage.
[09:58] Priya: Will do.
[10:00] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. Ending at 3:52 — I'll follow up with calendar invite for routing deep-dive.

End of transcript.
